title: SQC and Schneider Electric deploy hybrid quantum-classical models for energy forecasting
key_facts: Silicon Quantum Computing (SQC), an Australian company, and Schneider Electric tested SQC's quantum-enhanced 'Watermelon' chip to improve household energy forecasting.

In the first stage, applied to next-day forecasting data over 12 months, the approach improved forecast accuracy by an average of 20 percent against a classical benchmark, with gains up to 41 percent.
The Australian government is giving A$3.6 million (US$2.5 million) so the project, run with UNSW Sydney, can move to stage two of its Critical Technologies Challenge Program.
Stage two will test hundreds of Australian homes and connect the quantum system directly to Schneider Electric's existing workflows.
The target problem is predicting energy demand and supply as homes add rooftop solar, batteries and electric vehicles.
Watermelon was launched in 2025 and is used for telecoms, banking and high-frequency trading; it can be accessed by cloud or bought as hardware.
The article says stage two will test whether the gains from the first trial hold when moving from a limited dataset to hundreds of real homes.
quote_evidence: During the first stage of the program, researchers applied Watermelon to next-day energy forecasting data covering a 12-month period.
Compared with the classical benchmark, the quantum-enhanced approach produced an average 20% improvement in forecasting accuracy, with improvements reaching as high as 41%.
The second stage will test the technology on a much larger dataset covering hundreds of homes across Australia.
why_it_matters_hint: Better home energy forecasts could help manage rooftop solar and batteries, but the accuracy figures are the partners' own and not independently reviewed.
event_date: Stage 2 funding announced about 1-2 Oct 2026 (Dealroom item 1 Oct 2026 23:41 UTC; Quantum Insider and Interesting Engineering 2 Oct 2026); stage 1 results cover a 12-month data period.
notes: Original Computer Weekly blog blocked (403 Cloudflare). Same story read at Interesting Engineering; The Quantum Insider (press release text) read and agrees on all figures. Results come from a press release by the two companies; no independent check reported.
